**Finding submitted: deviation (medium severity, TRANSITION).**

What I found:
- **Transition assistance — exceeds preferred.** Section 11.3 makes our right to serve then-existing Customers survive indefinitely, and Section 5.3/11.3 make Commerce One's support and maintenance obligations survive termination (subject to our annual fees). Section 12's source code escrow adds further continuity. No redline needed here.
- **Data return — fails the fallback.** The only exit data provision is the mutual Confidential Information clause in 11.3, which lets Commerce One elect to *destroy* our information, with no return obligation for data of Corio, its Customers or Software Users held on the MarketSite.net Service, no machine-readable format, no 30-day deadline and no deletion certification. Permitting outright destruction of our data sits in walk-away territory.

Redline (validated, ok:true): a single narrow insert of new Section 11.4 requiring (a) up to six months' transition assistance at then-current rates, (b) return of our and our Customers' data within 30 days in a commonly used machine-readable format, and (c) deletion thereafter with written certification, subject to legal retention — with a stated willingness to fall back to 90 days of assistance.
